newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: INSIGHT-Australia 10-yr bond stuck in the range.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Australia 10-yr bond stuck in the range.

text.p: *The Australian 10-year bond futures contract ended SYCOM with a minor gain, remaining entrenched in its recent 93.360/93.470 range.
*U.S. Treasuries ended firm, benefitting from an early slide in U.S. stocks, and despite a late rebound in the share market.

The September Australian 10-year bond futures contract ended after-hours trading with a minor gain, remaining entrenched in its recent 93.360/93.470 range and still looking for a decisive break after last week's shake-out.
The contract ended SYCOM at 93.400 and up from Monday's soft open outcry close of 93.385.

On the downside 93.360 has proved suppportive after last week's rebound from 93.135, but equally approaches to 93.470 have proved resilient and where a break is needed to resume the rally to the all time high of 93.695 set on August 1.
Firm U.S. Treasuries helped to underpin the market in SYCOM.

The U.S. market benefitted from a stronger U.S. dollar and asset allocation switching as U.S. stocks were hit again in early trade on Monday. It held firm going into the close despite the equity market rebounding strongly by the finish.
The Dow Jones industrial average finished 109 points higher after dropping 83 points at one stage in the wake of Friday's 247 point sell-off.

Locally, the key event will be the Reserve Bank's quarterly bulletin at 3.00 p.m. (0500 GMT) which will be heavily scrutinised for any further clues on policy after last week's less hawkish than expected speech by governor Ian Macfarlane.

In the U.S. the Federal Open Market Committee meets later on Tuesday but no change in monetary policy is expected given the recent flow of friendly inflation data and other signs that the economy is not over heating.

Fears of an imminent tightening in German monetary policy, which has recently hit the U.S. dollar, were dampened on Monday after Bundesbank council member Hans-Juergen Krupp said that a hike in rates would severely damage the German economy.
The Bundesbank conducts its latest repo tender later on Tuesday and the central bank council meets on Thursday.
